title: Tenant SLA: Game of Throttles — Simulation Cookbook and Operator Notebook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview This page documents the "Game of Throttles" simulation cookbook — a repeatable laboratory for exercising tenant-level throttling, burst-credit consumption, and graceful degradation policies before they reach production. The intent is to give platform operators and engineers: - A set of reproducible scenarios for capacity stress and fairness experiments. - A compact operator playbook for running simulations and interpreting dashboards. - Templates for alerts, dashboards, and postmortem artifacts to accelerate learning cycles. Audience and scope - Primary: Platform operators, SREs, and runtime engineers. - Secondary: Product and account teams who want to validate tenant behavior under enforced SLAs. - Scope: Multi-tenant inference clusters (Redwood Dedicated and Hosted API routing surface). This cookbook focuses on request-level throttling, token-burst semantics, and tenant priority slices. It explicitly excludes hardware-level noisy-neighbor mitigation (covered by GPU fleet runbooks). Goals and success criteria - Validate that priority-tier throttles preserve high-tier SLOs while limiting high-volume low-tier tenant cost exposure. - Exercise fallback/eviction policies without compromising data isolation or observable traces. - Produce repeatable dashboards and artifacts usable in QBRs and capacity planning. Key definitions (operational) - Fair Share Score: synthetic score used in the simulation combining recent token consumption, error rate, and latency deviation (0-100). - Burst Token Bucket: tenant-level bucket (size B, refill R/sec) used to model short-term surges. - Soft-throttle: best-effort rate limiting that returns 429 with Retry-After but still allows critical heartbeats. - Hard-eviction: forcibly migrate or cold-stop a tenant workload when safety thresholds breach for N seconds. Ownership and roles | Role | Responsibility | On-call contact | | Operator lead | Coordinate simulation, runbooks, operator safety controls | @operator-oncall | | Experiment author | Design scenarios and verify metrics instrumentation | @runtime-eng | | Customer liaison | Communicate expected impact to affected customer teams | assigned account manager | | SLO owner | Validate SLI changes against acceptance criteria | @slo-owner | Simulation components - Traffic generator: sandbox-client (python) that supports per-tenant token-rate profiles and injected percentile latencies. - Controller orchestrator: simctl (CLI + small REST service) to stage scenarios and toggle policy knobs (burst size, refill, priority weights). - Observability stack: dashboard templates (Grafana), synthetic SLI exporter, and trace correlation keys (sim_id). - Safety net: circuit-breaker flag in the allocator and immediate rollback job. Required preconditions 1. Lab namespace created and tagged 'sim-game-of-throttles-'. 2. Operator kube RBAC role with simctl write permissions. 3. Billing sandbox isolated; tests must not touch production billing meters. 4. Canary capacity reserve (10% of region pool) set aside for operator-initiated compensations. Metrics and SLI matrix - SLI: 95th token-generation latency (ms) — per-tenant and global. - SLI: Error rate (5xx/total) — per-tenant. - SLI: Token throughput (tokens/sec) — per-priority tier. - Derived: Fair Share Delta = (median fair_share_score of top tier) - (median fair_share_score of bottom tier). Acceptance thresholds for a successful simulation run: - Top-tier 95p latency increases by <15% vs baseline. - Bottom-tier median latency may increase but healthy fallback preserved (errors <2% additional). - No tenant experiences data-plane isolation violations (checked via trace sampling). Simulation recipes (repeatable) 1) Baseline capture (10–15 minutes) - Start simctl with an empty overlay: simctl init --env lab --note baseline.
- Run traffic generator with profile 'steady' for 10 minutes across 100 synthetic tenants. - Record metrics and save dashboard snapshot (tag sim_id). 2) Short-burst storm (burst size B=1e6 tokens) - Configure: simctl set-policy --burst-size 1000000 --refill 2000 --policy soft-throttle - Trigger: pick 10 low-priority tenants and ramp token rate 10x for 60s. - Observe: burst bucket depletion, token leakage, and retry-after patterns. - Operator checks: are high-tier latencies within threshold? If not, abort and rollback. 3) Sustained overcommit (graceful eviction exercise) - Configure: reduce global allocator headroom to 80% and set eviction-safety N=120s. - Trigger: ramp 15 medium-tier tenants to 2x sustained traffic for 15 minutes. - Observe: allocator decisions, proactive rebalancing, and eviction events. - Safety: if >3 hard-evictions occur, pause simulation and collect heap/profile artifacts. 4) Mixed-priority worm (fairness stress) - Configure: weighted scheduler (weights: top 100, medium 20, low 5). - Trigger: flood low-priority tenants uniformly for 20 minutes while generating light top-tier traffic. - Observe: fair-share delta and priority-weight enforcement. Operator playbook (runbook steps during a live sim) 1) Pre-run checklist (30 minutes before): - Confirm lab namespace, RBAC, and canary reserve. - Announce maintenance window to internal channels (Slack #platform-sim). - Verify dashboard widgets for sim_id are visible and alerts muted for the lab group. 2) During run (real-time): - Monitor top-tier 95p latency and fair-share delta every 60s. - If Fair Share Delta > configured alert threshold (default 40): increase soft-throttle aggressiveness (simctl set-policy --scale 1.5) and re-evaluate. - If any high-tier errors spike >1% absolute over baseline: trigger immediate soft rollback (simctl rollback --to baseline). 3) Emergency abort (criteria): - Hard-evictions > 3 OR high-tier SLO breach maintained for >120s. - Steps: set allocator to safe-mode: simctl allocator --set safe; notify account managers; run kill-switch to drain simulation traffic; collect diagnostics. 4) Post-run artifact collection (automated) - simctl export --sim-id --artifacts metrics,traces,profiles > /tmp/sim--bundle.tar.gz - Upload to artifact store with naming sim-game-of-throttles/. Attach to the retrospective ticket. Dashboard and alert templates - Dashboard essentials: - Row: Sim overview (sim_id, policy knobs, tenant counts). - Row: Per-tier latency pctiles (50/95/99) with drift bands. - Row: Burst bucket occupancy heatmap. - Row: Fair Share Delta timeseries and histogram. - Example alert thresholds (lab defaults): - alert_sim_high_tier_latency: 95p_top_tier > 1.15 * baseline for 60s -> Sev2 -> notify @operator-oncall - alert_sim_fairshare_skew: fair_share_delta > 40 for 120s -> Sev3 -> paging disabled (notify Slack channel) - alert_sim_hard_eviction_rate: hard_evictions >= 1 within 5min -> Sev1 -> immediate abort recommended Templates (CLI/JSON) - Sample simctl start command: - simctl start --env lab --name "game-of-throttles-" --policy-file policies/worm-mix.json --note "fairness-experiment" - Minimal policy JSON (inline example): - {"policy_name": "worm-mix", "burst_size": 1000000, "refill": 2000, "priority_weights": {"top": 100, "medium": 20, "low": 5}, "eviction_safety_seconds": 120} Safety and guardrails - Always run in a sandboxed billing environment. If a test touches billing APIs, abort immediately and notify finance. - Any test that produces hard-evictions must be accompanied by a scheduled cleanup window and postmortem. - Operators must not change production allocator knobs during a lab run. All knob changes must be through simctl which enforces lab scoping. Post-simulation retrospective checklist 1. Attach exported artifacts to the retrospective ticket. 2. Run automated diff vs baseline for core SLIs and save as CSV. 3. Fill the experiment template: objective, hypothesis, steps taken, observed results, owner, follow-ups. 4. If policy changes are recommended, create RFC/ADR and list rollback criteria. Roadmap and follow-ups (engineering asks) - Q1 2026: Add a synthetic tenant generator that can replay real traffic traces while anonymizing PII. - Q2 2026: Integrate simctl with the sandbox cost meter to provide real-time burn-rate feedback. - Q3 2026: Expose a limited UI in Console for experiment scheduling and visibility for platform PMs. Appendix - Quick commands and locations - simctl status --sim-id # show live status - simctl snapshot --sim-id --save ./snap.json - Artifact store: s3://redwood-platform-sim-artifacts/game-of-throttles/ - Dashboards: Grafana link (internal) -> Dashboard id: platform-sim-overview-42 Related reading - See tenant-eviction-simulator-operator-playbook-2026 for eviction operator templates. - Review capacity-futures-operator-runway-roadmap-2027 for alignment with upcoming allocator changes. Contact and feedback - Author: Aisha Patel (runtime-eng). For run scheduling or questions open a ticket in the Platform Simulation epic or ping #platform-sim on Slack. Change log - 2025-09-16: Initial draft and lab validation. - 2025-12-02: Added emergency abort criteria and artifact automation. - 2026-01-18: Updated acceptance thresholds and roadmap items.
